headline: Hackers claim data of 19m Pathao users, demand $400,000 ransom
summary: A group of hackers alleges to have compromised the personal data of 19 million Pathao users. They are demanding a hefty sum of $400,000 to prevent the release of this sensitive information.
details: A hacker group has publicly claimed to have breached the systems of Pathao, a popular ride-sharing and delivery service in Bangladesh. The group asserts they have accessed the personal data of approximately 19 million users, a significant portion of the company's customer base.

To prevent the alleged stolen data from being leaked or sold, the hackers have issued a ransom demand. They are reportedly seeking $400,000 in exchange for the return or deletion of the compromised information.

While the specific types of data claimed to be compromised were not detailed in the initial reports, such breaches often involve user names, email addresses, phone numbers, and potentially other personal identifiers. Users are advised to remain vigilant regarding their online security.

Pathao has not yet officially confirmed the breach or responded to the hackers' claims. The incident raises serious concerns about digital security and the protection of user privacy for millions in Bangladesh.

headline_marked: [[DP World to operate Chattogram's New Mooring Container Terminal]] for 15 years, deal signed amid protests
headline: DP World to operate Chattogram's New Mooring Container Terminal for 15 years, deal signed amid protests
summary: The Dubai-based firm will manage the largest terminal at Chattogram Port, handling 44% of its container traffic, with an investment of over BDT 1,000 crore for modernization. The deal, however, sparked protests from labor organizations.
details: Chattogram Port Authority has signed a 15-year agreement with Dubai-based DP World to operate the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT). The government-to-government (G2G) deal under a public-private partnership (PPP) was finalized after a long process initiated with an MoU in 2019.
The agreement was signed at the Invest Bangladesh office in Agargaon, Dhaka. Rear Admiral Md Moniruzzaman, Chairman of Chattogram Port, and Essa Kazim, Chairman of DP World, signed the deal.

NCT is the largest of Chattogram Port's four operational terminals, handling 44% of the port's total import-export container traffic. Completed in 2007, the nearly one-kilometer-long terminal can accommodate four ocean-going and one smaller container vessel simultaneously.

The signing ceremony in Dhaka was met with protests outside by several left-leaning organizations, including CPB and BASAD, which police dispersed with batons. Separately, port labor organizations in Chattogram also protested, announcing a mass hunger strike for Monday if the deal is not cancelled.

Labor unions have been opposing the lease of NCT to a foreign operator since the interim government, arguing that NCT is a profitable terminal. Despite government assurances that workers will not be harmed, concerns persist regarding job security and national interest.

Under the agreement, DP World will invest over BDT 1,000 crore in modernizing the terminal, equipment, and technology within the first 10 years. Chattogram Port will receive an upfront fee of approximately BDT 600 crore, with 25% paid upon signing and the remainder before operations begin.

Invest Bangladesh stated that Chattogram Port will receive 40% to 67% of the revenue based on container handling income tiers. DP World is obligated to handle at least 1.23 million TEUs annually, a target considered achievable given last fiscal year's 1.385 million TEUs at NCT.
